analysis_notes.source_text_structure: Torah #268 is a short teaching (3 paragraphs) structured entirely as eitza (cause-and-effect) argumentation. It contains no explicit bechina language ('הוא בחינת', 'נקרא', 'כנ"ל') anywhere in the text. The argument is: (1) a person who ignores the תכלית has no reason to live; (2) the נפש yearns to do God's will — when it sees the person failing, it withdraws toward its שורש, causing illness; (3) when a person takes medicine he demonstrates he can subdue his תאוה for some purpose — the נפש sees this and hopes he will do the same for the true purpose (God's will), so it returns. All relationships are sequential/causal, not parallel/shared-nature.

eitza_chains_identified.chain: אי-הסתכלות על התכלית → נסיגת הנפש לשרשה → חולי
eitza_chains_identified.description: Not looking at the ultimate purpose causes the soul to withdraw toward its root, causing illness

eitza_chains_identified.chain: כפיית התאוה (לצורך רפואה) → ציפיית הנפש → חזרת הנפש → בריאות
eitza_chains_identified.description: Subduing desire for medicine shows capacity to subdue desire; soul sees this and returns; person recovers

eitza_chains_identified.chain: כפיית התאוה לתכלית האמתי → עשיית רצון יוצרו
eitza_chains_identified.description: The implied eitza — if the person subdues desire for the true purpose (God's will), complete healing of body and soul follows

analysis_notes.note_on_bechina_absence: The absence of bechina language in Torah #268 is significant: this is a practical/mussar-style teaching that operates through logical argument rather than through the identification of parallel essences across domains. The concepts נפש, תכלית, תאוה, and רפואה function as actors in a causal narrative, not as bechina-equivalents. Consequently, the dataset correctly has zero bechina edges for this Torah. The proper data representation for this Torah would consist entirely of eitza edges.
